# Baselines

*Generated by `scripts/build_report.py` from `results/baselines_*.json`. Do not edit by hand.*

Every baseline is newly implemented in `adexec/policies.py`; none is inherited from the upstream repository. Tuning used only the 4,000 in-distribution episodes of the TRAIN split (split tag 11). That is the same in-distribution information the RL agent is trained on; neither saw a shifted market. All candidates were scored on identical episodes (common random numbers).

| Policy | Form | Tuned parameters | Grid / budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| TWAP (fallback) | sell remaining / steps left | none | — |
| AC | static Almgren-Chriss sinh trajectory (κ<0: mirrored back-loading) | κ | 25-point grid on [−3, 3] |
| ADAPT | TWAP-remaining × exp(−a·signal + b·depth − c·spread − d·rv + e·volume), clipped to [¼, 4] | a, b, c, d, e | coordinate descent, 3 rounds, 25-point grid on [−3, 3] per weight (≤ 361 evaluations) |
| A3 blend | w·RL + (1−w)·TWAP per step | w | {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} on validation (LOFO) |
| A9 rule gate | fall back if rv, spread or size > TRAIN-ID q-quantile, or depth or volume < (1−q)-quantile | q | {0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99} on validation (LOFO) |
| A10 random | fall back with RCG's per-condition, per-replicate rate | none (matched) | exact expectation |

## Tuned values

| Impact model | AC κ | AC train IS (bp) | TWAP train IS (bp) | ADAPT weights (a, b, c, d, e) | ADAPT train IS (bp) | ADAPT evaluations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sqrt | -1 | 7.082 | 7.095 | (1.5, 0.5, 1.25, -0.75, 0.25) | 5.071 | 362 |
| linear | -0.75 | 6.225 | 6.231 | (0.75, 0.25, 0.5, -0.25, 0.25) | 5.031 | 362 |
| transient | -1.25 | 7.030 | 7.044 | (2.0, 0.5, 1.75, -1.0, 0.5) | 4.753 | 362 |

Under the risk-neutral IS objective, tuned AC is practically identical to TWAP: train IS differs by about 0.01 bp. This is what theory predicts. With zero risk aversion the Almgren-Chriss optimum is the uniform schedule, and the small selected κ ≠ 0 reflects noise in the selection. We keep AC in every table for completeness, but the meaningful classical baselines are TWAP (static, robust) and ADAPT (feature-driven, strong).

**Grid-edge check.** The first ADAPT grid ([−1, 1]) put the signal weight on its boundary, and so did a second ([−2, 2]) under the transient model. To avoid handicapping the baseline, the grid was widened to [−3, 3] before any RL policy was evaluated. All selected weights are now interior.
